correctness.rationale: For independent Bernoulli p_i in [0,p], 0<p<=1/2, derive P(S=2)/P(S=0)=e_2(p_i/(1−p_i)). At fixed pair sum s=x+y and product v=xy, e_2=H+[Us+(1−2U)v]/(1−s+v); its derivative in v is [1−s−(2−s)U]/(1−s+v)^2. If e_2>=1, the contrary nonnegative derivative would force e_2<1 using H<=U²/2 and s<1, a contradiction. Thus reducing v at fixed s strictly increases e_2 and saturates one interior probability per step, reaching m full-cap parameters and one residual q. The saturated e_2 crosses 1 at minimal m with binom(m+1,2)(p/(1−p))²>=1; q=(1−binom(m,2)t²)/(mt+1−binom(m,2)t²), threshold T=mp+q. Strict compression establishes boundary uniqueness, perturbation gives sharp strict-event infimum; p=1/2 and p→0 limits verified. Independent exact-rational grid tested 6552 instances over six caps and lengths ≤6, including threshold and equality families. Testing is finite only.
